meh: It does what was asked, in the way a wet sock keeps a foot covered.
The customer says it is fine, twice, and looks at it a third time on the way out.
Done. The less said about the middle part, the better.
good: It does the job, and the job stays done.
The customer nods, pays, and does not come back with it.
Solid work. It will not be the talk of the town, and it will not need mending.
Exactly what was asked for, which is rarer than it sounds.
great: The customer smiles before remembering to haggle.
It is good enough that someone asks who made it.
A proper piece of work. The customer carries it out with both hands.
Better than asked. The customer pretends not to notice, badly.
perfect: The customer goes quiet, which in this town is high praise.
It is worth talking about, and by supper people are.
Nobody could have done it better, and the goose next door agrees.
The customer leaves to fetch a friend, to show them.
